recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Reintroducing a non-normative label would be inappropriate because the hData section is gone; no follow-up is needed unless a future work group decision intentionally reintroduces hData guidance.
issue_request: Published FHIR-core/FHIR-I STU3 change request resolved Persuasive with Modification. The issue questioned whether the HTTP page's OMG hData section implied a normative alternative transport and resolved to remove the hData section.
initial_application: No current git commit explicitly mentions FHIR-16458, but source/http.html history shows the hData section was commented out by 6c524e959315a07f484862bbcd627c2ce90a3057 shortly after the June 2018 vote and then deleted by 996a1f3590fd9b32e1883f47b977b26a3e98234b before the Jira comment saying it was already done.
additional_context: Current source/http.html is the RESTful API page and contains no hData, OMG Health, projecthdata, or hData RESTful Transport section. A later public Zulip hData thread is consistent with removal because Grahame Grieve stated that FHIR no longer claimed consistency with hData. No Confluence references or conflicting community evidence were found for the issue.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. No source edit was made because the requested section is absent from current build source.
